newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Costly S.Africa export scheme to be axed July 11.
newsitem.headline: Costly S.Africa export scheme to be axed July 11.

text.p: A controversial South African export promotion programmes will be axed on July 11, after it cost the state an estimated 10.3 billion rand, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Department of Trade and Industry financial assistance schemes director Emile Matthee told Reuters that final claims under the General Export Incentive Scheme (GEIS) were expected to reach the department by October 30.
He said that 2,500 claims valued at 441 million rand were currently outstanding and it was difficult to estimate claims still to be received.
But the total cost of the programme since 1990 had been around 10.3 billion rand.
"The scheme could have been a greater success if it was not so general in nature," Matthee said.
"It lacked focus and was not targeted. Although it stimulated exports of manufactured products, the bulk of the benefits probably went to existing exporters who did not need it," he said.
Matthee said it seemed that manufacturers had accepted the decision to end GEIS, which was announced in April.
They had been warned over a number of years that GEIS was counter to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and World Trade Organisation commitments.

GEIS, a cash payment based on free on-board export values, was introduced to counter the anti-export bias that had been built up in South African manufacturing by years of high tariff protection during the apartheid era.
"Many of the elements of anti-export bias have been alleviated considerably, which should enable firms to be more competitive," Matthee said.
These included lower tariffs on inputs, export rebates, a real depreciation of the exchange rate, improved market access and the expansion of the export marketing assistance scheme.
At the same time, so-called "supply-side" measures had been introduced to retrain staff and improve productivity.
